definitions.gloss: way of perceiving; interpretation; how one looks at something
definitions.explanation: The manner in which someone understands, interprets, or grasps a concept, situation, or problem. Formed from the verb {捉|とら}える (to grasp/perceive) plus {方|かた} (way of doing).

examples.japanese: {捉|とら}え{方|かた}は{人|ひと}それぞれだ。
examples.english: Everyone has their own way of looking at things.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}の{捉|とら}え{方|かた}を{変|か}えてみよう。
examples.english: Let's try changing the way we look at things.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}じ{出来事|できごと}でも、{捉|とら}え{方|かた}によってポジティブにもネガティブにもなる。
examples.english: Even the same event can seem positive or negative depending on how you interpret it.

notes:
USAGE:
A common abstract noun in discussions about perspectives, attitudes, and mindset. Often used in self-help, psychology, and everyday conversation about reframing problems.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {捉|とら}え{方|かた}を{変|か}える (to change one's perspective)
- {捉|とら}え{方|かた}によって (depending on how you look at it)
- {捉|とら}え{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う (to have a different interpretation)
- {物事|ものごと}の{捉|とら}え{方|かた} (way of looking at things)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {考|かんが}え{方|かた}: way of thinking — broader, about thought processes in general
- {見方|みかた}: viewpoint, perspective — more about visual or evaluative perspective
- {解釈|かいしゃく}: interpretation — more formal, used for texts or rules
